g1.label: 1. The main reason ___ this idea
g1.why: The writer “strongly agrees”, so the reasons must support the idea — keep the position consistent.

g2.label: 2. ___, a single extra course can make a graduate more useful
g2.why: This sentence is a result of the point before it, so it needs a result linker.

g3.label: 3. A second argument ___ compulsory courses
g3.why: The paragraph gives another reason to support the courses: an argument in favour of them.

g4.label: 4. ___, some students may feel …
g4.why: “Admittedly” introduces the other side before the writer answers it with “However”.

g5.label: 5. ___, I believe …
g5.why: The final paragraph sums up the essay, so it starts with a concluding phrase.

g6.label: 6. the benefits clearly ___ the costs
g6.why: To match “strongly agree”, the benefits must be greater than the costs: they outweigh them.

g1.label: 1. ___, they are flexible
g1.why: The second sentence adds another advantage, so it needs an addition linker.

g2.label: 2. ___, many people still prefer to drive
g2.why: Preferring to drive is surprising after “cheap”, so it needs a contrast linker.

g3.label: 3. ___, more people began cycling
g3.why: Cycling more is a consequence of higher fuel prices, so it needs a result linker.

g4.label: 4. Software development, ___, is often done remotely
g4.why: Software development is an example of a job done from home.

g5.label: 5. ___ the high cost
g5.why: “Despite” is followed by a noun phrase (the high cost); “although” needs a full clause.

g6.label: 6. ___ the course was difficult
g6.why: A full clause (the course was difficult) after a contrast needs “although”.

g7.label: 7. ___ cities have grown
g7.why: “Whereas” compares two opposite facts in one sentence.

g8.label: 8. It ___ reduces stress
g8.why: Reducing stress is a second benefit, so it is an addition: also.

g1.correct: Another benefit is that courses outside a student’s field teach practical skills.
accept: Another benefit is that courses outside a student’s field teach practical skills.
g1.label: 1. Paragraph on languages and coding skills
g1.why: The paragraph gives two examples of practical skills; the topic sentence must name that main idea, not one detail.

g2.correct: Investing in cycle lanes is one of the most effective ways to reduce traffic.
accept: Investing in cycle lanes is one of the most effective ways to reduce traffic.
g2.label: 2. Paragraph on cycle lanes
g2.why: The paragraph explains how cycle lanes cut traffic; the other options are off-topic or too general.

g3.correct: Part-time work has both advantages and disadvantages for students.
accept: Part-time work has both advantages and disadvantages for students.
g3.label: 3. Paragraph on part-time work
g3.why: The paragraph gives one benefit and one problem, so the topic sentence must cover both sides.

g4.correct: Online learning makes education more accessible.
accept: Online learning makes education more accessible.
g4.label: 4. Paragraph on online lessons
g4.why: Both details show more people being able to learn — the idea of accessibility.

g5.label: 5. Review (Task 1): fell ___ 52% to 35%
g5.why: “From … to …” gives the start and end figures — from the Writing Task 1 exercise.
